purposes.command.document.object.layer.compositin: Edit layer blend mode, mattes and opacity compositing.

resourceBoundary.policy: Complete correlated retained receipt or typed refusal. The request is one flat edit of one layer and is at most 4096 encoded bytes, so a full effect stack that does not fit is refused, never split.

semantics: #2372: the baseline layer compositing writes of src/js/timeline.js and src/js/effects-panel.js @1065e9d8 as one native transaction per edit (the owner is scene_effect_layer_edit.rs). edit blend: picking Normal clears the member. matteMode: sets the first matte's mode, optionally freezing the source in the same write (the matte menu freezes the adjacent layer); the menu's None is matteClear, which removes the first matte and its additional mattes. matteSource: picking a source on a layer with no real mode sets alpha. matteMoreAdd/Set/Remove: the additional mattes (adding needs a matte that is on; removing the last removes the member). effects: replaces the layer's complete effect stack, so add, remove, reorder and toggle each send the full resulting stack; effectsFromSet/Clear borrow another layer's stack. folderCollapsed: folder layers only; it is saved with the layer as one revision but adds no history entry and leaves redo alone (the baseline disclosure toggle pushed no undo snapshot). A layer cannot matte itself or borrow its own stack; named layers must exist. blendKeySet / blendKeyRemove / blendKeysClear: the hold-only keys of an animated blend mode (the Blend stopwatch of src/js/motion.js @1065e9d8, layerBlendModeAt). blendKeySet puts the mode at a frame (`index` carries the frame; a key already there is replaced; the frame must be inside the project); the mode holds until the next key, nothing is interpolated, and the stored blend is ignored while keys exist. blendKeyRemove removes the key at a frame (not_found when none; removing the last key removes the member). blendKeysClear is the stopwatch off: it drops every key and, when it carries a mode, makes that mode the static blend in the same write (Normal clears it), as the baseline does when the only key is removed. blendKeysMove / blendKeysRemove: the group forms of the key grid (a drag or Alt+Arrow nudge, and Delete, over the selected Blend diamonds of one layer). `frames` names 1 to 64 existing keys, strictly increasing (not_found when one is no key). blendKeysMove shifts them by the non-zero `by` frames with their modes (baseline onDragMove / nudgeSelectedKeys): every target must be a frame inside the project that no staying key holds, else the whole move is refused (invalid_request) and nothing changes. blendKeysRemove removes them all (removing the last key removes the member). A group of keys is still one history entry and one revision. One successful edit is one history entry and one revision (except the folder chevron, above); an edit that leaves the layer equal publishes nothing. Hover previews of the blend and matte pickers are UI-local and never reach this operation. No JS/Paper writer or fallback.
